from machine import Pin
import framebuf
import time


class SSD1351:
    def __init__(self, spi, dc, cs, rst):
        self.spi = spi
        self.dc = Pin(dc, Pin.OUT, value=1)
        self.cs = Pin(cs, Pin.OUT, value=1)
        self.rst = Pin(rst, Pin.OUT, value=1)
        self.rst(0)
        time.sleep_ms(10)
        self.rst(1)
        time.sleep_ms(10)
        for c, a in ((0xFD, b'\x12'), (0xFD, b'\xB1'), (0xAE, b''), (0xA0, b'\x74'), (0xA1, b'\x00'), (0xA2, b'\x00'), (0xA6, b''), (0xAF, b'')):
            self._cmd(c, a)

    def _cmd(self, c, data=b''):
        self.cs(0)
        self.dc(0)
        self.spi.write(bytes([c]))
        if data:
            self.dc(1)
            self.spi.write(data)
        self.cs(1)

    def text(self, s, x, y, colour=0xFFFF):
        w = 8 * len(s)
        buf = bytearray(w * 8 * 2)
        fb = framebuf.FrameBuffer(buf, w, 8, framebuf.RGB565)
        fb.text(s, 0, 0, colour)
        # framebuf stores RGB565 little-endian; the SSD1351 wants the high byte first.
        for i in range(0, len(buf), 2):
            buf[i], buf[i + 1] = buf[i + 1], buf[i]
        self._cmd(0x15, bytes([x, x + w - 1]))
        self._cmd(0x75, bytes([y, y + 7]))
        self._cmd(0x5C, buf)

from machine import Pin, SPI
from ssd1351 import SSD1351
import time
spi = SPI(1, baudrate=20000000, sck=Pin({SCL}), mosi=Pin({SDA}))
tft = SSD1351(spi, {DC}, {CS}, {RES})
time.sleep(1)
tft.text('HELLO 42', 10, 40)
